name: Lutetium
blurb: Lutetium reaches MR as hardware and as a therapy label, not as a spin: LSO and LYSO crystals in PET/MR detectors are lutetium oxyorthosilicate, and their 2.59 % 176Lu makes every crystal self-radioactive at roughly 300 Bq per cm3. 177Lu (6.64 d) is the beta emitter in Lutathera and Pluvicto, so lutetium patients now routinely get MRI for lesion dosimetry.
mrNotes: 175Lu is 97.4 % abundant with I = 7/2 and gamma 4.847 MHz/T (14.5 MHz at 3 T), but Q = +349 fm2 is among the largest in the periodic table, so lutetium NMR is a solid-state and NQR technique.
The 176Lu background in LSO/LYSO sets the singles-rate floor of a PET/MR detector and is exploited for on-line gain and energy calibration.
Lu3+ is 4f14 and diamagnetic, so unlike Gd3+ or Dy3+ it produces no paramagnetic relaxation enhancement; natLu chelates are the cold surrogate used to work out 177Lu radiochemistry.

No frequency ratio is quoted for 176Lu: with I = 7 and Q = +492 fm2 no solution measurement could anchor one, and the tabulated value is inconsistent with every published moment. The 175Lu ratio is sound; the 0.17 % gap against the gamma here is only the difference between the 2025 recommended moment and the older one that IUPAC's own entry still carries.

isotopes.notes: Xi = 11.404 % is sound and is not the odd number here: IUPAC's own lutetium entry carries gamma = 4.86258 MHz/T, which is the pre-2025 moment +2.2327, and that moment reproduces Xi with a shielding of +1445 ppm, the expected sign and size for a closed-shell 4f14 Lu3+ ion. The 0.17 % gap against the gamma quoted here appears only because this chart uses Stone's 2025 recommended +2.2257, which is 0.31 % lower. Q = +349 fm2 (Pyykko 2018 agrees).

I = 7 is the highest ground-state spin of any naturally occurring nuclide. Beta emitter, 3.76e10 y; the source of the intrinsic count rate in LSO and LYSO PET crystals and of the Lu-Hf geochronometer. No frequency ratio is given: Xi = 8.131 would imply a moment between +3.179 and +3.184, two to three standard deviations above the measured +3.1692(45) and 0.6 % above the +3.160 used here, and with I = 7, Q = +492 fm2 and 2.59 % abundance no solution measurement could underpin a ratio for it.
Therapy nuclide of 177Lu-DOTATATE and 177Lu-PSMA-617; 208 keV and 113 keV gammas allow SPECT dosimetry. Nanomolar clinical concentrations are far below any NMR detection limit.

name: Hafnium
blurb: Hafnium has two NMR-active isotopes and no NMR: 177Hf and 179Hf pair small gyromagnetic ratios (1.72 and 1.08 MHz/T) with quadrupole moments above 330 fm2, and no hafnium resonance has been reported in solution. Its clinical appearance is HfO2 nanoparticles injected as a radiotherapy dose enhancer, which are dense on CT and silent on MR.
mrNotes: 177Hf sits at 5.2 MHz and 179Hf at 3.2 MHz in a 3 T magnet, below the tuning range of most broadband probes.
179Hf has a negative magnetic moment (mu = -0.6389, I = 9/2), so its gamma is negative and its receptivity is only 0.43 times 13C despite 13.6 % abundance.
HfO2 radioenhancer nanoparticles (NBTXR3) are diamagnetic in effect, add no measurable R1 or R2, and are tracked by CT rather than MR.
The IUPAC frequency ratios for 177Hf and 179Hf are mutually consistent to about 100 ppm but imply gamma values roughly 1 % below those from Stone's moments.

isotopes.notes: I = 7/2, Q = +337 fm2. Receptivity 1.5 times 13C on paper, but quadrupolar broadening has kept the nucleus effectively unobserved.
Negative moment, so gamma = -1.082 MHz/T. Q = +379 fm2 is the largest quadrupole moment in group 4 and the practical barrier to observation.

name: Tantalum
blurb: Tantalum is the radiopaque implant metal of neurointervention and orthopaedics: aneurysm clips and coil markers, trabecular metal acetabular cups, cranioplasty mesh and radiostereometry beads. It is Pauli paramagnetic with a volume susceptibility near +180 ppm (SI) against tissue at about -9 ppm, so it distorts the local field but feels no force in the bore.
mrNotes: 181Ta is 99.988 % abundant with I = 7/2, gamma 5.133 MHz/T (15.4 MHz at 3 T), Xi = 11.9896 % and a nominal receptivity 216 times 13C, but Q = +317 fm2 broadens solution lines beyond use; NQR and solid-state MAS are the working methods.
Tantalum markers are not ferromagnetic; the artifact is a susceptibility-driven signal void that blooms with TE and with B0, typically a few millimetres at 3 T for a 1 mm bead.
180mTa, 0.012 % of natural tantalum, is the only nuclear isomer found in nature and the only natural nuclide with I = 9; its half-life exceeds 4.5e16 y.
Porous tantalum implants heat less than long conductive leads because they are compact; the RF concern with tantalum hardware is geometry, not the metal.

isotopes.notes: Xi = 11.9896 % implies gamma 5.1049 MHz/T, 5560 ppm below the 5.1333 MHz/T from Stone's moment, consistent with the absolute shielding of a heavy 5d metal.
180mTa, the naturally occurring isomer; the ground state has an 8 h half-life and is absent from nature. I = 9 with Q = +480 fm2, of interest to nuclear structure rather than NMR.

name: Tungsten
blurb: Tungsten is the shielding, collimator and septa metal of nuclear medicine and the radiopaque core of guidewires, coils and embolic markers. 183W is a genuine spin-1/2 NMR nucleus in polyoxometalate chemistry, but at 1.78 MHz/T (5.3 MHz at 3 T) and 0.062 times the receptivity of 13C it is almost always detected indirectly through 1H or 31P.
mrNotes: 183W: I = 1/2, 14.31 % abundant, Xi = 4.166387 % against 1 M Na2WO4 in D2O at pD 9; direct observation takes hours, so INEPT and HMQC transfer from 31P is standard in polyoxotungstate work.

W(CO)6 falls near -3500 ppm on the tungstate scale while polyoxotungstate lines cluster within a few hundred ppm of the reference, so individual tungsten sites in Keggin and Dawson anions are resolved.
Tungsten alloy (about 95 % W) is the standard syringe shield, collimator and PET septum material; chi_molar = +59e-6 cm3/mol makes it non-magnetic in handling terms.
The 188W/188Re generator supplies 188Re for bone and liver therapy; 188W itself has I = 0 and no NMR signal.

isotopes.notes: gamma is so small that even at 21.1 T the 183W frequency is only 37.6 MHz. T1 in diamagnetic complexes runs to minutes, so relaxation agents or polarization transfer are used for direct observation.

name: Rhenium
blurb: Rhenium is a nuclear medicine element rather than an MR one: 186Re (3.72 d) and 188Re (17.0 h, eluted from a 188W generator) are beta emitters used for bone pain palliation, radiosynovectomy and liver therapy. Both naturally occurring isotopes have large gyromagnetic ratios near 9.7 MHz/T and receptivities in the hundreds relative to 13C, but Q above 200 fm2 means only very symmetric species such as ReO4- give an observable line.
mrNotes: 187Re is the rhenium nucleus of choice: 62.6 % abundant, Xi = 22.7516 % against KReO4 in D2O, 29.2 MHz at 3 T, and a marginally smaller Q than 185Re.
Stone's 2025 moments (+3.1570 and +3.1888) come from a 2022 re-measurement and sit about 0.9 % below the values behind older published gamma tables.
Rhenium is the cold congener of technetium, so 99mTc radiopharmaceutical structures are normally established on the analogous Re complexes and checked by 1H and 13C rather than 185/187Re NMR.
The two isotopes give a textbook pair: their Xi values and Stone moments agree on absolute shielding to within 5 ppm, which is the best internal consistency check in this row.

isotopes.notes: Beta emitter with a 4.12e10 y half-life, the basis of Re-Os dating; effectively stable for spectroscopy. Q = +207 fm2 keeps linewidths in the kHz range outside tetrahedral ReO4-.
Slightly larger Q than 187Re and lower abundance, so its line is both weaker and broader; rarely the nucleus chosen.
Beta and gamma emitter (137 keV) for bone pain palliation and radiosynovectomy; mu = +1.728, diamagnetically corrected. Not an NMR nucleus.
Eluted from a 188W generator; 2.12 MeV beta endpoint with a 155 keV imaging gamma. mu = +1.777. Not an NMR nucleus.

name: Osmium
blurb: Osmium offers two NMR nuclei of opposite character: spin-1/2 187Os, which gives sharp lines across several thousand ppm but has a receptivity of only 0.0014 times 13C, and quadrupolar 189Os, about 1700 times more receptive yet broad outside OsO4. Osmium arene complexes are studied as anticancer metallodrugs, normally with 187Os enrichment and 1H-detected correlation.
mrNotes: 187Os: I = 1/2, 1.96 % abundant, gamma 0.974 MHz/T (2.9 MHz at 3 T); it is one of the least receptive nuclei in the periodic table and is essentially never observed directly.
Os(II) arene and cyclopentadienyl complexes fall between -2000 and -5200 ppm on the OsO4 scale (Xi = 2.282331 %, OsO4 in CCl4).
189Os (I = 3/2, 16.15 %, Q = +86 fm2) is only narrow enough for a high resolution probe in the tetrahedral OsO4 molecule itself.

Both isotopes are referenced to the same molecule, so Xi(189)/Xi(187) must equal (mu189/I189)/(mu187/I187) with the shielding cancelling. The tabulated ratios give 3.40240 and the tabulated moments 3.43036, 0.82 % apart, so at least one of the four numbers is wrong; rounding of the three-figure 187Os moment accounts for less than a tenth of it.

isotopes.notes: Receptivity 2.3 times 13C, far better than 187Os, but quadrupolar relaxation restricts observation to OsO4. No frequency ratio is given: the tabulated 189Os and 187Os ratios cannot both be reconciled with any published pair of osmium moments, and since both are referred to the same OsO4 line the discrepancy cannot be shielding. The 187Os ratio is kept because the osmium shift scale is quoted on it.
Moment known to only three figures, so the derived gamma carries about 0.2 % uncertainty. Practical spectra come from 187Os-enriched samples and 1H-187Os HMQC.

name: Iridium
blurb: Iridium is NMR's blind spot: 191Ir and 193Ir have gyromagnetic ratios of 0.76 and 0.83 MHz/T, among the smallest of any stable nuclei, and no iridium resonance has ever been recorded in solution. Clinically iridium shows up as 192Ir, the 73.8 d source of HDR brachytherapy, and as the Pt-Ir alloy of stimulation electrodes and embolisation coils.
mrNotes: 191Ir and 193Ir resonate at 2.3 and 2.5 MHz at 3 T, below the tuning range of a normal broadband probe, with receptivities of 0.063 and 0.14 times 13C.

The IUPAC frequency ratios (1.718 and 1.871 %) imply gamma values about 4 % below those from Stone's moments and disagree with each other by 0.4 %; the iridium entries in the unified scale are not experimentally anchored.
192Ir (73.83 d, I = 4, mu = +1.924, Q = +215 fm2) is the workhorse HDR brachytherapy source; the afterloader hardware, not the source, is what enters an MR suite.
Pt-Ir raises the radiopacity and stiffness of electrodes and coils without making the alloy ferromagnetic, so the MR issue is susceptibility artifact and lead heating, not attraction.

isotopes.notes: More abundant and slightly more receptive than 191Ir, and still unobserved in solution. Q = +75.1 fm2. No Xi is given: iridium has never been observed by solution NMR, so a frequency ratio for it would be an estimate rather than a measurement.

Used in nuclear resonant scattering and Mossbauer work rather than NMR. Q = +81.6 fm2. No Xi is given: iridium has never been observed by solution NMR, so a frequency ratio for it would be an estimate rather than a measurement.
HDR brachytherapy gamma source (mean photon energy about 380 keV). I = 4, mu = +1.924; no NMR role.

name: Platinum
blurb: 195Pt is the one broadly useful NMR nucleus in this group: spin 1/2, 33.8 % abundant, Xi = 21.496784 % (27.6 MHz at 3 T), 20 times the receptivity of 13C, and a chemical shift range near 15000 ppm that resolves every ligand substitution at the metal. Platinum is also the electrode and embolisation coil metal of implanted devices, with a volume susceptibility near +280 ppm (SI) against tissue at about -9 ppm.
mrNotes: Xi = 21.496784 % against 1.2 M Na2PtCl6 in D2O puts 195Pt inside the range of a standard broadband probe at every clinical and spectroscopy field.

Cisplatin resonates near -2100 ppm on the PtCl6(2-) scale; the practical detection limit for platinum drugs is around 500 uM, orders of magnitude above tissue concentrations, so there is no in vivo 195Pt MRS.
195Pt chemical shift anisotropy runs to thousands of ppm, which shortens T1 and T2 at high field and forces fast MAS or wideline methods in the solid state.
Platinum and Pt-Ir aneurysm coils, stents and electrode arrays are not ferromagnetic; the limits are RF heating of attached leads and a local signal void, not translational force.

isotopes.notes: The only NMR-active platinum isotope. 1H-195Pt and 15N-195Pt correlation is the standard way to characterise platinum drugs at low concentration.

name: Gold
blurb: Gold is the contact, fiducial and nanoparticle metal that NMR cannot see: 197Au is 100 % abundant but has the smallest gyromagnetic ratio of any stable nucleus, 0.738 MHz/T (2.2 MHz at 3 T), marginally below 191Ir, combined with Q = +54.7 fm2. Gold is diamagnetic (chi_molar = -28e-6 cm3/mol), so gold markers give a compact signal void with no force or torque.
mrNotes: 197Au NMR is a solid-state technique confined to cubic environments such as gold metal, where the quadrupole coupling averages away; there is no accepted solution reference compound.
Receptivity is only 0.15 times 13C despite 100 % abundance, and Xi = 1.729 % places the resonance below the tuning range of most broadband probes.

Gold fiducial markers for image guided radiotherapy are visible as a focal void on gradient echo images; a 1 mm by 3 mm cylinder blooms by a few millimetres at 3 T and is better localised with short-TE or UTE sequences.
198Au (2.69 d, I = 2, mu = +0.5934) is the beta emitter of historical colloidal gold therapy and of current radioactive gold nanoparticle work.

isotopes.notes: Q = +54.7 fm2 (Stone 2013 and Pyykko 2018 agree). Knight-shifted metal resonance in bulk gold is the main reported observation.
Beta emitter with a 412 keV gamma; used in colloidal 198Au therapy and in radiolabelled gold nanoparticles. No NMR role.

name: Mercury
blurb: 199Hg is a spin-1/2 nucleus with a workable gamma of 7.71 MHz/T (23.1 MHz at 3 T) and about 5.9 times the receptivity of 13C, which makes it the standard probe of mercury binding in metallothionein and other thiolate proteins. Optically pumped 199Hg and 201Hg vapour cells serve as comagnetometers in neutron electric dipole moment experiments; metallic mercury itself is diamagnetic, and the old MR suite hazard was the steel in sphygmomanometers, not the mercury.
mrNotes: 199Hg: 16.87 % abundant, Xi = 17.910822 % against neat HgMe2, the IUPAC primary reference; shifts run roughly -3000 to +1000 ppm.
Hg(II) thiolate sites in proteins fall between about -100 and -1000 ppm, and two-, three- and four-coordinate geometries are separable by shift alone.
201Hg (I = 3/2, 13.18 %, Q = +38.7 fm2) has a negative moment and resonates at 8.5 MHz at 3 T, but quadrupolar broadening keeps it out of routine use.
203Hg (46.6 d, I = 5/2, mu = +0.849) was the label in chlormerodrin renal scanning and survives only as a laboratory tracer.

isotopes.notes: Large chemical shift anisotropy, so solid-state lines need MAS; in solution 199Hg T1 is short enough for rapid repetition.
Negative moment, gamma = -2.847 MHz/T. Its Xi and that of 199Hg imply absolute shieldings agreeing to 80 ppm, a good internal consistency check.
Beta emitter with a 279 keV gamma; the historical chlormerodrin renal agent. No NMR role.

name: Thallium
blurb: 205Tl is the third most receptive spin-1/2 nucleus after 1H and 19F, about 830 times 13C and twice 31P, with gamma 24.88 MHz/T so that it resonates at 74.6 MHz at 3 T, close to protons in a 1.75 T magnet. Tl+ is a potassium mimic of almost identical ionic radius, which makes 205Tl a direct probe of K+ sites in nucleic acids and enzymes and makes 201Tl the classic myocardial perfusion SPECT tracer.
mrNotes: 205Tl: Xi = 57.683838 %, 70.5 % abundant, receptivity about 830 times 13C, so a single scan suffices at millimolar concentration.
Shifts span more than 6800 ppm, from [TlI4]- near -1730 ppm to Me3Tl near +5090 ppm on the aqueous TlNO3 scale, so 205Tl reports coordination directly.
Tl+ (1.50 A) substitutes at K+ sites (1.38 A); 205Tl NMR has been run in erythrocyte suspensions and perfused hearts, but there is no whole-body in vivo 205Tl MRS.
201Tl (3.04 d, I = 1/2, mu = +1.599) is imaged by its 68 to 80 keV mercury X-rays after electron capture, not by NMR.

isotopes.notes: IUPAC prints the reference as Tl(NO3)3 in H2O, which is unstable; the scale is in practice anchored on aqueous TlNO3 at infinite dilution. Dissolved O2 broadens Tl+ lines by tens of Hz.
Chemically identical to 205Tl but 2.5 times less receptive; used mainly to confirm assignments through the isotope pair.
Myocardial perfusion SPECT tracer taken up through the Na+/K+ ATPase. I = 1/2, mu = +1.599; NMR-active in principle, invisible at tracer level.

name: Lead
blurb: 207Pb is a spin-1/2 nucleus with gamma 9.00 MHz/T (27.0 MHz at 3 T), 22.1 % abundance and about 12 times the receptivity of 13C, and it carries a chemical shift range near 16000 ppm, among the widest of any spin-1/2 nucleus; Pb2+ substitutes at Ca2+ and Zn2+ sites, which makes it a direct structural probe of those metalloproteins. Lead is also the X-ray shielding metal of the imaging department, diamagnetic itself, so lead aprons and shielded inserts are limited by weight and by their steel fittings.
mrNotes: 207Pb: Xi = 20.920599 % against neat PbMe4; reported shifts run from about -5030 ppm to +10745 ppm and are dominated by relativistic spin-orbit effects, so prediction needs four-component theory.
Chemical shift anisotropy frequently exceeds 1000 ppm, so even 10 to 20 kHz MAS leaves large sideband manifolds; the anisotropy itself is the structural observable.
Pb(NO3)2 is the standard MAS rotor thermometer, its 207Pb shift moving +0.753 ppm per K.
212Pb (10.6 h) feeds 212Bi in targeted alpha therapy but has I = 0 and no NMR signal.

isotopes.notes: The only NMR-active lead isotope. Long T1 in diamagnetic organolead compounds, short T1 and enormous shifts in lead chalcogenides where Knight-shift-like terms dominate.

name: Bismuth
blurb: 209Bi is 100 % abundant with I = 9/2 and a receptivity of about 840 times 13C, the highest of any nucleus in period 6, yet it is barely usable in practice because Q = -42.2 fm2 and low site symmetry give kilohertz linewidths even in simple salts. Bismuth is the most diamagnetic metal (chi_molar = -280e-6 cm3/mol), it is used in bismuth shields for CT breast and eye dose reduction, and 212Bi and 213Bi are alpha emitters for targeted alpha therapy.
mrNotes: Xi = 16.069288 % against Bi(NO3)3 in HNO3, which is 20.8 MHz at 3 T; that reference line is itself about 4.4 kHz wide even at 360 K, limiting frequency determination to roughly 1 ppm.
Stone's 2025 moment (+4.092) reflects the 2018 re-measurement that resolved the bismuth hyperfine puzzle and is 0.45 % below the older +4.1106 behind most published gamma tables.

Q = -42.2 fm2, from bismuth diatomics with full-Dirac CCSD(T) field gradients (Dognon and Pyykko 2023); the world average over modern atomic and molecular determinations is -42.0(1.7) fm2. This supersedes the -51.6 fm2 of Stone 2013 and of Pyykko's own 2017 table, a 20 % revision that rescales every quadrupole coupling derived from the older value, and the other bismuth isotopes with it, since their moments were measured as ratios to 209Bi.
209Bi NMR and NQR are used on topological insulators such as Bi2Se3 and on bismuth intermetallics, where site symmetry is high enough to narrow the line.

isotopes.notes: Alpha decay with a 2.01e19 y half-life was detected in 2003, so 209Bi is the longest-lived radionuclide rather than a stable one; for spectroscopy it is stable. Receptivity about 840 times 13C, just ahead of 205Tl, though 93Nb, 51V and 27Al are higher still.

Targeted alpha therapy nuclide eluted from a 225Ac/213Bi generator; 440 keV gamma allows imaging. mu = +3.717. Q is given here as -67.9 fm2: the older -83 fm2 rescaled by the 2023 revision of the 209Bi moment, since the other bismuth quadrupole moments were measured as ratios to it. That is a rescaling, not a measurement.
